name: Lino decals
subtitle: Carved ravens, crows, bats and Pan in one colour of vinyl.
tags: lino linocut carving vinyl decal pan goat raven crow bat sticker cutting weeding
description: Carve a raven, crow or bat into closed shapes for cutting from one colour of vinyl. Choose a die-cut figure, a moon or a carved block, then change the gouges, silhouette and scale.
lesson: The filled shapes are the vinyl you keep; the holes are what you weed away. Export the decal cut layer from the studio, set it to Basic Cut in Design Space and check the size in millimetres. Iron-on exports are already mirrored by the studio; do not mirror them a second time. Physical cut sizes remain untested.

name: Spider web
subtitle: Orbs, tangled corners, moonlit hedges.
tags: spider orb cobweb sheet dew moon hedge silk nature
description: Grow an orb between twigs, fill a corner with cobwebs, or stretch a sheet web through the grass. Add dew, torn threads and a spider at the hub.
lesson: Frame threads and radii support the capture spiral. Different web types change the construction; twig and leaf outlines hide threads behind them. Dew can use a separate pen.

name: Weather
subtitle: Thunderheads, valley fog, pressure charts.
tags: weather sky clouds storm lightning rain fog isobars fronts map snow
description: Build weather over a stack of ridges, or switch to a chart of pressure systems, fronts and wind barbs. Rain, cloud cover and wind have their own controls.
lesson: Landscape views clip rain and cloud marks against foreground shapes. Chart views use a pressure field for isobars and separate symbols for fronts and wind. These are generated scenes, not forecasts.

name: Orrery
subtitle: Invented planets. Brass arms. Binary suns.
tags: space planets astronomy orbits stars solar system brass binary moons
description: Draw a seeded star system from above, tilt its orbital plane, or mount its planets on the arms of a brass orrery. Planet portraits and textbook plates use the same controls.
lesson: The seed chooses a fictional system. View, rings, moons and orbit styles change its presentation; the brass view adds mechanical arms. It is a drawing generator, not an orbital simulation.

name: Island atlas
subtitle: Survey sheets, treasure maps, portolans.
tags: island map cartography survey contour treasure antique portolan atoll terrain
description: Make an island, archipelago or atoll and draw it as a survey sheet or an old chart. Add contours, rivers, settlements, compass roses and a route to buried treasure.
lesson: A seeded height field supplies the coast and relief. Survey views show contour levels; antique views add mountain symbols and coastal lines. Rhumb lines and water can use a separate pen.

name: Underground
subtitle: Roots, tunnels, fungi, things left buried.
tags: earth soil roots mycelium fungi mushrooms burrows fossil geology core strata ants
description: Slice through a meadow to find roots, mycelium and burrows. Choose a broad section, an isolated block or a set of cores; tuck a fossil or a lost object between the layers.
lesson: Ground layers and foreground objects hide the marks behind them. Root density, fungal growth and tunnels are separate controls. Core samples and block sections expose different parts of the generated soil.

name: Archaeology studio
subtitle: Trench sections, site plans, sieves and refits.
tags: archaeology excavation trench section stratigraphy site plan findspots sieve pottery refit sherds midden posthole
description: Draw a trench section through layers and cuts, a site plan with findspots and contours, a finds sieve, or a broken pot laid out for refitting.
lesson: Sections follow excavation conventions: layers, cuts and fills read top down. Plans mark findspots against a grid. Refits break a seeded vessel into sherds and can leave pieces missing.

name: Flint studio
subtitle: Handaxes, blade cores, arrowheads, scrapers.
tags: flint lithics knapping handaxe levallois blade core arrowhead scraper flake stone age illustration plate
description: Knap a stone into a handaxe, a blade core, a Levallois flake, an arrowhead or a scraper, then draw it as a lithic illustration plate or a reduction sequence.
lesson: Each flake removal leaves a scar with ripples running away from the strike point. The method decides the order of removals; marks and arrows can go on a second pen to show the knapping sequence.

name: Pottery puzzle
subtitle: Decorated pots broken into sherds to rebuild.
tags: pottery puzzle sherds pot vessel beaker amphora decoration cut layer board refit jigsaw
description: A decorated pot drawn in pen and broken into sherds on the cut layer, with a board sheet to rebuild it on. Pick a tradition or compose the decoration band by band.
lesson: The pen layer carries the decoration and the cut layer carries the breaks, so one sheet makes the puzzle pieces. Sherd count and missing pieces set the difficulty. Cut sizes are untested.

name: Spirograph
subtitle: Layered wheels, odd rollers, gardens of rosettes.
tags: spirograph wheel gear loops rings letters words heart star flower rosette pattern colour pens hypotrochoid epitrochoid
description: Wheels roll round a word or a shape and the pens in their holes draw the loops. Stack four wheels on one track, swap in oval, triangle or wavy rollers, or scatter a whole garden of rosettes across the page.
lesson: The wheel's centre follows the outline at a distance of one radius, so a big wheel skips the narrow gaps a small one gets into. The wheel turns once per circumference of travel; the radius is nudged so the pen closes after the chosen laps, each lap landing in a new place.

name: Math garden
subtitle: Pendulums, growing words and the edge of the Mandelbrot set.
tags: math maths mathematics harmonograph pendulum lissajous rotary l-system lindenmayer plant tree fractal koch snowflake dragon curve hilbert sierpinski gosper mandelbrot julia contour lines escape time
description: Three ways to grow a drawing out of a rule. A harmonograph swings two damped pendulums against each other until the pen spirals to a stop. An L-system rewrites a word over and over and a turtle walks it as plants, snowflakes and space-filling curves. A Mandelbrot or Julia set is drawn as contour lines, the way a map draws hills.
lesson: A pendulum that loses a fixed share of its swing every second fades exponentially, so the loops close in evenly; a frequency ratio of small whole numbers closes into a figure, and a hair of detune makes it walk round. A contour line joins points that escape equally fast, so the lines crowd where the set's edge is busiest.

name: Vampire paper doll
subtitle: Fangs, a tailcoat and a cape on the shoulder pins.
tags: seasonal halloween spooky vampire dracula count nosferatu fangs cape paper doll jointed split pin jumping jack cut layer toy
description: A jointed vampire drawn in pen and cut into parts with a pin hole at every joint: the Count, a little vampire or Nosferatu, with a tall-collared cape that rides on the shoulder and neck pins behind the body.
lesson: The cape is cut with holes at exactly the doll's shoulder and neck joints, so it shares their split pins and hangs still while the arms swing in front of it. The body is the jointed figure studio's own rig, so the paper doll wardrobe's clothes fit it too.

name: Spooky garland
subtitle: Ghosts, pumpkins and bats to string up.
tags: seasonal halloween spooky garland bunting ghost pumpkin jack-o-lantern bat window string hanging hole cut layer
description: Charms to cut out and string across a window, each with a hanging hole at the top or two for the string to weave through. Jack-o-lantern faces are drawn and filled in by the pen, or cut right through so the light shines out.
lesson: Every charm is one distance field: pumpkin lobes, a ghost's dome and wavy hem, a bat's scalloped wings. A cut-through face is subtracted from the same field, and the studio checks that every strip of card left between a face and the edge is at least 2 mm wide.

name: Poison apple
subtitle: The poured coat is the skull; the apple shows through.
tags: seasonal halloween spooky inktober apple poison candy apple tattoo flash traditional drips skull worm banner bite
description: A poison apple for Inktober. The poured coat is the skull: sockets and a nose open as holes in it, the apple shows through, and the coat runs off the jaw in drips like teeth. One slider takes it from a candy apple to a rotten, melting skull, in black ink with sunburst rays, as a colouring page, or as a colour tattoo with arched lettering.
lesson: Two layers: an apple underneath and a coat on top, and the skull is only the coat. The coat is one distance field, everything above a jaw edge smoothly merged with a row of drips, minus two tilted sockets and a nose that points up; wherever the coat is not, the apple shows.

name: Jointed figures
subtitle: Cut-out dolls and jumping jacks on split pins.
tags: paper doll jointed figure jumping jack puppet skeleton robot knight bear split pin cut layer toy
description: A skeleton, robot, knight or bear drawn in pen and cut into parts with a pin hole at every joint. Pin it together with brass paper fasteners as a posable doll, or string it as a jumping jack. Cut sizes untested.
lesson: Each part is a few rounded shapes merged into one outline, and every joint is a disc of card round a hole at the same point on both parts. A jumping jack's limbs have a tab past the pivot: pull the tabs down and the limbs swing up.

name: Paper Dolls / Paper Clothes
subtitle: Everyday dolls: clothes, hair, hats, and gangly concertina limbs.
tags: paper doll paper clothes wardrobe outfit dress coat shirt trousers skirt shoes boots hair braids ponytail hat crown tabs split pin concertina gangly inktober cut layer
description: The everyday tab of the Paper Dolls / Paper Clothes studio: T-shirts, jumpers, shirts, dresses, coats, trousers, shorts, skirts, shoes, boots, eight hairstyles, five expressions, three hats and things to carry for the plain doll from the jointed figure studio, or a gangly doll with concertina arms and legs cut on the same sheet (Inktober day 16, gangly). Cut sizes untested.
lesson: Each garment is the doll part beneath grown by 1.2 mm and trimmed to shape. Where it covers a joint it shares the doll's split pin; where it does not, fold tabs wrap behind the doll.

name: Jointed animals
subtitle: Rabbits, horses, dogs and more, on split pins.
tags: animal jointed rabbit horse zebra dog dalmatian cat elephant pig split pin cut layer toy spots stripes
description: A rabbit, horse, dog, cat, elephant or pig in side view, cut into a body, a nodding head, a wagging tail and four legs pinned in pairs. Spots, stripes or patches turn a horse into a zebra and a dog into a dalmatian. Cut sizes untested.
lesson: Each outline is a smooth curve through hand-placed points, and the pen adds fur strokes that follow the body and engraved shading along the undersides. Near and far legs share one split pin at the shoulder and one at the hip, so walking them apart reads as a stride.

name: Worlds
subtitle: Star systems from a seed, and the life of every world.
tags: space planets star system exoplanet red dwarf binary two suns atlas world lava ocean ice desert gas giant moons rings life astronomy seed
description: A seed makes a planetary system: a red dwarf’s close family, a sun with rock inside and giants outside, worlds round two suns. Read its atlas, or stand on one world and follow its life from molten rock to the end of its sun.
lesson: Worlds form as rock inside the frost line and as gas and ice outside it; warmth comes from starlight and distance, and small hot worlds lose their air. When moves the clock: low shows the newborn system, past 1 shows its future. The rules are rough on purpose; it is a drawing generator, not a model.

name: Forks
subtitle: A copied mind: its family tree, its upload, its code.
tags: posthuman transhuman fork merge copy clone identity lineage genealogy upload mind consciousness code personhood theseus profile head self
description: What happens to a self that can be copied. Draw its lineage as a family tree of forks and merges, move it across in an upload slice by slice, or fill a head with the lines of code it runs on.
lesson: Every head is one profile curve nudged by a seed, so each fork drifts a little from its parent and the shading shows how far it has come from the original. The upload asks the ship of Theseus question three ways: replace it slice by slice, copy it beside itself, or let the original dissolve as the copy forms.

name: Meatsack
subtitle: Bolt on, swap out, print another.
tags: posthuman transhuman cyborg cybernetics augmentation implant prosthetic patent drawing replacement theseus clone clones vat body parts serial
description: The literal side of being posthuman. Draw an augmentation as an old patent sheet with numbered parts, replace a body part by part from the hands inward, or line up clones in their vats with one original among them.
lesson: The body is built from rounded shapes merged by a distance field, so every part has its own outline. A replaced part keeps that outline and swaps contour hatching for panel seams, rivets and joint discs, which is all it takes to read as machine next to flesh.

name: Cipher garden
subtitle: Mazes, tiles, ridges. Messages stashed inside.
tags: tiles maze ridgelines constellation knots code
description: A message becomes a landscape, a constellation or a field of tiles. Follow the marks and the drawing tells you what it says.
lesson: The drawing is the code. In Truchet tiles, orientation carries a bit; in ridgelines, the line carries the message. Different methods need different reading keys.

name: Gear weave
subtitle: Sunflowers, chainmail, swarms of gears.
tags: woven chainmail sunflower swarm gears texture
description: Hundreds of toothed rings pass over and under one another. Order a lattice, grow a sunflower, or let the whole thing swarm.
lesson: Where two gears overlap, the rim passes over on one side and under on the other. Arrangement, size variation and fill change the entire character.

name: Signal book
subtitle: Flags, semaphore, ogham, braille.
tags: flags semaphore ogham braille tap code alphabet
description: Hoist a sentence. Draw an alphabet. Turn words into flags, gestures and marks, with black-ink hatching standing in for colour.
lesson: Signal flags use heraldic hatching to represent colour in black ink. Semaphore encodes letters through arm positions; ogham uses strokes along a stem.

name: Purloined plots
subtitle: Stitches, cables, punch cards.
tags: knitting stitches cables dots punch card textile hidden
description: A textile logic for hidden words: stitches, cables, dot charts and punch cards, all drawn in ink.
lesson: An encoding turns the message into symbols; a carrier decides how those symbols look. Changing the carrier changes the drawing while preserving its purpose.

name: Gear BAM!
subtitle: Extruded gears and comic lettering.
tags: comic typography lettering gears hatch dots riso
description: Extruded gears, crosshatched walls and a loud typographic punch. A small mechanical comic printed one line at a time.
lesson: Hatching and dots make tone from lines. The second pen layer can add a spot colour later; the geometry also works with black ink.

name: Overlay studio
subtitle: Moiré, masks and turning grilles.
tags: moire reveal visual crypto grille two sheets cut
description: Slide, stack or rotate a second sheet and something hidden comes into view. The interaction is part of the drawing.
lesson: These are physical, layered pieces. Moiré reveals need alignment; a turning grille exposes successive groups of letters. Check the studio instructions before plotting or cutting.

name: Machine relic
subtitle: Old hardware kept like a saint's bone.
tags: inktober relic reliquary jar preservation fluid cpu processor ram memory motherboard circuit board vacuum valve tube cables hoses wax seal cog halo sacred geometry binary machine cult cyberpunk transhuman tattoo flash
description: Inktober day 2. A processor, a memory stick, a broken motherboard or a vacuum valve hangs in preserving fluid inside a caged jar. Ribbed hoses and cables run out of it, wax seals hold strips of litany to the glass, and a cog, a saint's halo or sacred geometry stands behind, ringed with binary scripture.
lesson: Every part is a distance field drawn front to back, so each outline stops where something stands in front of it: the relic sits behind the cage bars and bubbles, and the cables start behind the jar. Dark areas are crosshatch at 0.75 mm, never a solid fill, so the pen lays an even tone without flooding the paper.

name: Miniature kit
subtitle: A model kit of a person, and the city in its chip.
tags: inktober miniature model kit sprue runner gates injection moulded plastic parts meatsack posthuman augments chip loupe magnifier isometric city architecture circuit die floor plan bus memory self cathedral
description: Inktober day 3. The Meatsack figure comes as a model kit, parts and augments held on the sprue by their gates. One part is a chip, and a loupe over it shows what the chip really is: an isometric city laid out like a die, with blocks named for memory, language, habit, fear and name, buses for roads and a cathedral core. Someone in it is holding a loupe of their own. Step four: insert self.
lesson: The kit is one distance field (frame, runners, gates and parts merged), so it outlines the way a moulded sprue does, and every part is held at two points. The city is drawn front to back with hidden lines, laid out as a chip floor plan, then cut to the lens and pushed through a bulge that magnifies the middle and squeezes the rim, the way glass does.

name: Cactus
subtitle: Cacti grown by their own rule, from seedling to bones.
tags: inktober cactus saguaro barrel column prickly pear opuntia echeveria succulent phyllotaxis golden angle fibonacci areole spines ribs desert night owl moon windowsill pots cochineal carmine skeleton bones botanical specimen label
description: Inktober day 4. Five scenes on one plant, and the windowsill can come with a cut-out window whose panes cut free round the plants: a specimen plate with a made-up Latin name and the areole spirals seen from above, a saguaro that ages from seedling through arms and bloom to torn skin, standing ribs and a heap of fallen rods, a windowsill of patterned pots, a desert night with an owl in a nest hole, and a prickly pear with the cochineal that make carmine.
lesson: Every areole turns the golden angle from the last, so the ribs and spirals settle into Fibonacci numbers by themselves. Spines leave each areole in 3D and are projected, so at the edges they point sideways; pads and rosettes use Vogel's sunflower spiral. A dying saguaro loses its skin to a noise field and shows the woody rods that were inside it all along.

name: Smack
subtitle: Nets that fold up, with art that meets itself over the edges.
tags: inktober smack net fold cube box die lantern jellyfish comic burst pow wham slap handprint ben-day dots speed lines cracks glue tabs score cut papercraft
description: Inktober day 5. A cube that took a hit: a comic burst or a slapping hand, speed rays and cracks running over its edges, a sound effect on each other face so it rolls as a die, glued shut or with a tuck lid. Or an open lantern wrapped in a smack of jellyfish, the ocean left as white paper and the bells cut out to let the light through.
lesson: The net is a tree of faces unfolded flat, with glue tabs on every edge it leaves open. The art is drawn in a development, several faces laid flat round one, then split face by face, so a line that leaves one end of the net comes back in at the other and meets itself once folded; the studio checks both halves on the folded solid.

name: Ogre jack
subtitle: A jumping-jack ogre whose pull string brings out the claws and a hidden RARRR.
tags: inktober ogre jumping jack paper doll split pins pull string monster roar rarrr speech bubble shout claws swamp cave baby posh tusks warts fish club onion teacup rattle cut
description: Inktober day 6. A plot-and-cut jumping jack ogre: at rest it stands there looking sheepish; pull the string and the bent arms swing up into claws over its head, the legs stomp out, and a spiky RARRR! bubble that was hiding behind its body swings out beside its head. Swamp, cave, baby or posh, with a fish, club, onion, teacup or rattle in the other hand.
lesson: Each part hangs with the centre of its area under its pin, so the rest pose is worked out, not drawn; an arm turns until its tab points straight down, and the bubble's tab is cut to the length that makes it finish on the same pull. The bubble sits on the back layer because its swing passes the shoulder pins, and a reveal on a jack has to come from behind, since the limbs hang behind the body.

name: Pan lino
subtitle: Pan, who gave panic its name, carved like lino and cut from one colour of vinyl.
tags: inktober panic pan goat god satyr horns pipes forest woods trees eyes lino linocut carving vinyl decal sticker cutting weeding
description: Inktober day 7. Pan, the goat-legged god who waited in the woods and frightened travellers out of their wits: standing with his arms folded or his pipes at his lips, peeking from behind a tree, or a block of night woods where he stands between two trees holding on to them, his horns up into the light and his eyes glinting out of the dark.
lesson: The same engine as the lino decals: drawn as filled curves, carved with gouges, cleaned to the vinyl rules and traced into one cut path. The filled shapes are the vinyl you keep; the holes are what you weed. Physical cut sizes remain untested.

name: Stink plume
subtitle: The smell is the drawing: it rises off something stinky and the flies loop through it.
tags: inktober stinky stink smell plume fumes pong streamlines flow field curl noise turbulence contour map cartoon stink lines corpse flower titan arum cheese stilton emmental sock fish fishbone kipper bin rubbish flies lifecycle age ripening bud bloom wilt collapse brie wheel mould
description: Inktober day 8. Something stinky at the bottom of the sheet (a corpse flower in its pot, a cheese on a board, an old sock that stands up by itself, a fish or a fishbone on a plate, a dustbin with its lid up) and its smell rising off it as pen lines: a plume that leaves smooth and breaks into swirls and dashes as it climbs, the cartoon stink lines that curl over at the top, or a contour map of the smell. Everything has an age: the corpse flower runs from bud to bloom to collapse, cheese ripens, a sock gets holier. Show one, or a row ageing left to right, each with its own plume. Flies loop through it.
lesson: The plume is a velocity field: straight up, spreading, bent by the wind, with curl noise faded in as it climbs, so the smell leaves the source smooth and turns turbulent higher up. Streamlines are seeded one spacing away from the lines already drawn and stop when they crowd another (Jobard and Lefer); widen the spacing with height and the smell thins out by itself, and plumes in a row share the grid, so they keep their spacing where they meet. Cheese eyes are packed biggest first and some are cut by the edge between two faces. Pen widths untested.

name: Ram skull
subtitle: Horns that grow like real horns, a ring a year, on a skull on its mount.
tags: inktober ram sheep skull horn horns spiral logarithmic growth rings annuli age trophy mount shield plaque wall overlay bighorn aries ovis memory ram chips circuit traces pcb cut out cutout board glue
description: Inktober day 9. A ram's skull on a shield, its horns grown the way real horns grow: horn is added at the base every year with a ring between, so the tip is the lamb's horn and an old ram's tip is broomed off by fighting. Hang a wall of mounts from lamb to old ram, lay the years over one skull in coloured pens, or put RAM on the ram: a memory chip for every year of horn, circuit traces over the skull and gold contacts at the snout. Add a cut line round the head, and plot the head and its board as separate sheets on different card, at the same scale, to cut out and glue together.
lesson: Each horn is a tube swept along a logarithmic spiral: it turns at a steady rate while its radius of curvature and its thickness shrink by the same factor, so every piece of horn is a scaled copy of every other. Tilted out from the face and flared sideways, it coils beside the skull. Hidden lines come from a depth buffer: every surface is rasterised at a quarter of a millimetre and each pen line is kept only where it is the nearest thing to the eye. Pen widths untested.

samples.title: The wall, lamb to old ram

name: Battering ram
subtitle: A siege ram to fold up: a gable-roofed shed and the beam that hangs through it.
tags: inktober ram battering ram siege shed gable roof wheels beam net fold papercraft box prism glue tabs score cut skull horns fleece memory ram stick chips circuit split pins wheels roll horns pose
description: Inktober day 9. A battering ram to cut, fold and glue: a shed with a gable roof on wheels that roll, and a beam with a ram's head on the end that slides through square holes in both gables. Plain wood (planks, shingles, iron bands), the ram all over it (a skull over the door, a fleece of curls on the roof, horns curled down the beam), or RAM: circuit-board walls and a beam that is a memory stick with gold contacts. The wheels and the ram’s horns are separate parts on split pins, packed into the spare card beside each net, so it rolls and the horns can be posed.
lesson: Built on the Smack studio's net engine: each solid is a list of faces in 3D, unfolded flat along a tree of folds, with glue flaps on every edge left open. The art is drawn in a frame on each face that knows which way is up once folded, so nothing ends up upside down, and the gable holes are a millimetre bigger than the beam so it slides. Cut and fold sizes untested.

samples.title: The shed, wheels to pin on
The beam as a RAM stick

name: Mystical
subtitle: A pair of paper hands and something mystical to do with it.
tags: inktober mystical hands crystal ball tarot cards tea cup leaves palm reading fortune oracle moon stars sigils rings bell sleeves cut out cutout layered backdrop paper hands glue foam
description: Inktober day 10. A pair of paper hands with bell sleeves hold, cradle or hover over a crystal ball, a tea cup read for its leaves, a fan of tarot cards or an open palm, on an arched night-sky backdrop. The backdrop, the object and the hands are three sheets on one page at one scale, with a cut line and glue guides, so cut out and layered the hands really do hold the thing.
lesson: Every piece is drawn on the same page at the same scale, so each cut-out drops back where it was drawn. The sky is left bare under the pieces that sit on it, apart from a thin rim, so a slightly crooked cut still hides the gap. Fingers bend in the plane of the page, and the poses are fixed so a pair of hands is always a believable pair. Pen widths and the narrowest cut untested.

name: Bottle
subtitle: A small apothecary: bottles, glass, liquid, and a label that says what you like.
tags: inktober rescue remedy bottle bottles apothecary potion tonic glass liquid cork stopper label shelf counter whimsy scribble label
description: Inktober prompt "rescue", day 11. Seven bottle shapes with liquid, glass shading and stoppers, five label shapes carrying your own title (it starts as Rescue Remedy), set as one bottle, a shelf of many or a potions countertop. A whimsy dial tips the bottles and bends the labels.
lesson: Glass is drawn as pen lines only: an outline, a liquid level with a meniscus and a few highlight strokes. Labels too small for lettering a pen can hold draw as scribble bars instead of text. Each shelf is a row of bottles that never overlap, with the nearer one cutting the line of the one behind.

name: Toss
subtitle: The same thing caught at several moments along its throw.
tags: inktober toss throw coin flip dice die roll graduation cap mortarboard multiple exposure motion study arc trail spin shadow
description: Inktober day 12. A coin, a die or a graduation cap caught at several moments along its arc, spinning as it goes, with a dashed trail, shadows on the ground and the last one landed. One throw, a pocketful of coins, a handful of dice or a whole graduating class.
lesson: Each thing is a small 3D model turned by one rotation per moment and projected flat, so the pips, the star and the reeded edge of a coin all foreshorten the way they should. Later moments sit in front of earlier ones and cut their lines, and the spin runs down to nothing at the landing so the last one comes to rest flat.

name: Flimsy bridge
subtitle: Six bridges folded from card, loaded, and drawn with what held.
tags: inktober flimsy bridge bridges truss pratt howe warren k truss bowstring plank card cardboard fold net cut out score statics tension compression buckling sag tacoma narrows galloping gertie 1940
description: Inktober day 13. Six ways across a gap, Pratt, Howe, Warren, K truss, bowstring and a bare plank, each a flat net to plot, cut and fold into a truss. A small solver loads every one and the pens draw the result: tension solid, compression dashed, the first member to go bowed or crossed, and the sag drawn on the deck. A second plate keeps the bridge that really was flimsy, the Tacoma Narrows, twisting itself apart.
lesson: Each truss is pin-jointed statics on centre lines, solved by the direct stiffness method: member force over member capacity gives the load the whole bridge holds. A card strut buckles long before it crushes, so the Howe, whose long diagonals are the compressed ones, holds about half what the Pratt does, which turns the same diagonals into tension. Stiffness and strengths are assumed until a strip of the real card has been pulled and bent.

name: Victorian lady
subtitle: A fashion-plate paper doll with three decades of gowns, hats and things to hold.
tags: inktober lady victorian paper doll fashion plate crinoline bustle leg-o-mutton gown dress evening ball suit corset petticoat bonnet hat parasol fan muff bouquet hair pompadour ringlets braids damask lace trim stand cut out fold tabs 1860 1885 1895
description: Inktober day 14. A lady with an hourglass figure in her corset, drawers and buttoned boots, who stands on an interlocking cross base and is dressed in gowns from 1860, 1885 and 1895: day dress, evening gown or walking suit, over a petticoat, with a capelet, a cameo choker, four hats, and a parasol, fan, reticule, muff or bouquet. Her hair is a sculpted updo, ringlets or a braided coronet, etched in fine strands.
lesson: Every garment is cut to her own outline grown by a millimetre and hung from fold tabs found by walking out from inside her edge until it leaves her, so the gowns fit her and only her. Hats tie on with ribbon strings that fold behind at the jaw. The cut sizes (tab width, the 1.2 mm notches, the thinnest bridge) are assumed until the cut calibration sheet has been read.

name: Hooray cards
subtitle: HOORAY cut through one pen pattern, drawn-on confetti cut from both panels, and a message card in corner slits.
tags: inktober hooray cards greeting card party congratulations layered card cut-away window stencil letters two patterns hatching stripes sunburst confetti sparkles waves zigzag polka dots three layers foam depth cast shadow confetti pocket offcuts envelope hearts stars smileys drawn-on confetti spirograph frame scallops message card corner slits
description: Inktober day 15. A card covered in one pen pattern with HOORAY cut through it, and a second pattern drawn on the coloured paper glued behind, so the word reads as a change of texture as well as colour. Add a middle layer and the front letters are cut a step bigger, so each letter gets a patterned rim. Hearts, stars and smileys are drawn on with the pen (faces, crosshatching, outlines) and then cut out of the front and the back panel, a frame and spirograph rosettes add more ink, and everything the blade lifts out goes into a printed pocket that says how many pieces of the card it holds. The message goes on its own card, in its own colour, tucked into four corner slits. Twelve patterns, your own words and an envelope from the same settings.
lesson: Every layer gets pen work and cuts: the pattern on each layer is clipped to stay clear of that layer's own cuts, and the layers behind are only drawn where the windows above can show them. Stencil letters keep a 2.6 mm bridge over each counter, windows keep 2 mm of card between them, confetti is at least 4 mm across, and the middle layer's letters are the front's letters shrunk by the step. Cut sizes are assumed until the cut calibration sheet has been read.

settings.headline: HOORAY
settings.inside: Proud of you. / Go and celebrate.

name: Contraption
subtitle: A parts kit and a chain solver: nonsense machines with real engineering, as a patent plate, a dimsa-doosa drawing or an exploded view.
tags: inktober contraption machine perpetual motion overbalanced wheel gears involute belts pulleys cam piston ratchet flywheel patent plate engineering drawing dimsa-doosa parts list balloons revision cloud exploded view hidden lines plausibility bureaucracy
description: Inktober day 17. A chain solver grows a machine one link at a time from a driver (an overbalanced wheel, a hand crank or a motor of unknown origin): gears meshed at the sum of their pitch radii, belts on the outer tangents of their pulleys, compound shafts, and driven things from a piston to a bell hammer. Every shaft carries its true speed, so the turning arrows and the output ratio are correct even when the machine is nonsense. Draw it as a perpetual motion patent plate, a dimsa-doosa engineering drawing with balloons, a parts list and revisions, or an exploded view. Plausibility breaks it on purpose, and bureaucracy buries it in paperwork.
lesson: A link is only kept if it clears everything already placed, and gear teeth are turned so a tooth faces a gap. Hidden lines on the exploded view come from drawing each part as a real extrusion.

name: Kiwi
subtitle: Shaggy kiwi alone under the ferns, stacked into a tower, tiled as wallpaper or packed in, with the odd kiwifruit.
tags: inktober flightless kiwi bird new zealand feathers tufts beak egg x-ray tower wallpaper packing kiwifruit ponga ferns koru moon southern cross night bush
description: Inktober day 18. A kiwi drawn from one pear-shaped outline roughened into hair-like tufts, with feather strokes hanging back from the head, a long curved beak with whiskers and nostrils at the tip, stout scaled legs, and a tiny wing hidden in the fluff or flapping, hopefully. Five poses, one kiwi with an egg beside her or an x-ray egg inside her, a tower of kiwi standing on each other's backs, a wallpaper grid or packed madness, with a dial that swaps some birds for kiwifruit. The night bush adds ponga fronds, koru, the moon and the Southern Cross in its real places.
lesson: Each part cuts the lines behind it, so the body hides the tops of the legs and a kiwi standing on another stands in its fluff. Tufts are sized in millimetres, so small and large birds look equally shaggy.

name: Confused deck
subtitle: Trading cards drawn as engineering drawings: no detail C, a blank sheet 2, "I dunno", grumpier sign-offs and a tolerance spinner.
tags: inktober confused engineering drawing title block trading cards technical design production rfi detail view sheet 2 lift flaps tolerance gd&t feature control frame spinner volvelle wheel brad red pen checker grumpy faces revision cloud stamps gag gift custom words
description: Inktober day 19. A deck of trading cards, each laid out as a production drawing with its own title block and each one a small drawing-office confusion. Lift detail C and there is no detail C, lift sheet 1 and sheet 2 is blank, ask the engineer and the answer is "I dunno", and watch the checker's red faces get crosser from who dimensioned this to WHO RELEASED THIS. The tolerance spinner turns a paper wheel behind a window in the dimension callout, mixing real callouts (H7/g6, ISO 2768-m, feature control frames) with unhinged ones (±0.0001 on a weld, datum D that does not exist). Every word is editable, so it makes a gag gift: names in the sign-off boxes, one tolerance on every card, and your own callouts on the wheel.
lesson: Flap hinges are scored and everything else is cut, with ink kept 0.4 mm off every cut and cuts at least 2 mm apart. The wheel's window starts far enough from the hub that a neighbouring callout never shows in it. Brad hole and cut sizes are assumed until the cut calibration sheet has been read.

name: Lounge
subtitle: A living room as a CAD floor plan at true scale, furniture as library blocks and the cats on a layer of their own.
tags: inktober lounge cats floor plan cad architecture blocks furniture sofa rug window seat sunbeam revision cloud rfi dimension scale layers block library
description: Inktober day 20. A living room drawn as a CAD floor plan at a true scale, its furniture placed as library blocks, and the cats on a layer of their own: lounging on the sofa, the rug, the window seat and in the sunbeam. A revision cloud, an RFI and a dimension to the star finish the sheet, and a block library sheet lays out every piece on its own.
lesson: Furniture is placed at its real size and the plan is scaled to the sheet, so a sofa always reads as a sofa next to the door. Cats sit on their own layer and pen, so they can be plotted in a second colour over the plan.

name: Dapper crows
subtitle: Crows on the wires in top hats, bowlers and boaters, waistcoats and cravats, under a crescent moon.
tags: inktober dapper crows birds wires telegraph hats top hat bowler boater waistcoat cravat cloth patterns moon night ball gossip murder
description: Inktober day 21. Crows lined up on telegraph wires, each dressed for the evening in one of five hats with a waistcoat and cravat cut from six cloth patterns. A murder of them, two gossiping, a duo, a moonlit row under a crescent moon sized to the free sky, or the whole flock at the ball.
lesson: Each crow is placed so it never overlaps its neighbour, and the moon is sized to the sky left between the wires. Cloth patterns are clipped to the waistcoat outline so the hatching never runs onto the feathers.

name: Beacon
subtitle: A prime-sized bitmap sent to the stars and a swarm that answers, or a LORAN chart with exact hyperbolic lanes.
tags: inktober beacon seti arecibo message bitmap prime radio dish array dyson swarm answer loran navigation chart hyperbola lanes coast contours ship fix waves
description: Inktober day 22. A message to the stars as a bitmap whose width and height are both prime, sent from Arecibo's bowl, a steerable dish or an array as rings that carry its bits, with a Dyson swarm that listens, opens a window or answers with a bitmap of its own. Or a LORAN chart: radio beacons on a generated coast with their time differences drawn as exact hyperbolic lanes, the waves that make them, and a ship fixing itself where two lanes cross.
lesson: The bitmap only decodes if its side lengths are primes, so the studio picks the grid from the message length. LORAN lanes are true hyperbolas with the stations as foci, and the coast is cut by marching squares so the contours never cross it.

name: Bletchley
subtitle: The people behind the code: a Bombe wall with Wrens' hands at the drums, a Wren drawn in Enigma letters, and the people of Station X.
tags: inktober hero bletchley park enigma bombe wrens station x code breaking hands cipher portrait letters official secrets act ww2 history people cast
description: Inktober, hero: the many people behind the code rather than one lone genius. A Bombe wall of 36 Enigmas stopped at the answer, with up to a dozen Wrens' hands at the drums and the menu ghosted behind; a Wren, name redacted, drawn only in Enigma letters; and the people of Station X, a different person and job for every number, singly or as a cast sheet. Their letters decode to the Official Secrets Act 1911, then a dedication, with the key printed underneath. A working Enigma is built in.
lesson: A face drawn in letters needs about sixty letters across before it reads, so cast sheets top out at four to a 12 x 12 sheet. Every portrait is checked by decoding its letters back to the message before it is allowed out.

name: Lightmap
subtitle: Render baking on paper: boxes with their shadows ray-traced into a lightmap, hatched on the boxes and flat in the UV atlas.
tags: inktober bake lightmap render baking ray tracing ambient occlusion sun shadows uv atlas unwrap seams boxes crates city cube hatching game art
description: Inktober day 24, bake: baking as in render baking. Boxes on a floor with their ambient occlusion and sun shadows ray-traced into a lightmap, drawn in hatching on the boxes and flat in the UV atlas beside them, each box unwrapped as a cross with its seams in colour.
lesson: The same lightmap texel drives both views, so a shadow on a box face lands in the matching square of its unwrapped cross. Hatching density follows the baked light, so darker texels get more lines rather than thicker ones.

name: Fracture
subtitle: An engraved world cracked like glass or torn down a seam, with its wireframe, code or circuit board showing through.
tags: inktober fracture reality glitch shatter glass tear rift posthuman transhuman cyberpunk wireframe code rain hex circuit board pixels halftone aliasing landscape mountains wanderer
description: Inktober day 25, fracture: an engraved world of mountains, hills, a cottage and a wanderer seen from behind, broken. Shattered like a pane of glass, the shards crowd toward the impact; some drift loose with hex address labels, some are rasterised into halftone pixels, and the innermost are gone. Or torn down a vertical seam, the two halves peeled apart like cloth with frayed crumbs falling into the gap. What shows through is what was always behind the picture: the landscape's own wireframe, falling code or a circuit board. Bits leak out on the wind past the frame, and glitch bands slip the world sideways.
lesson: Every shard is a real polygon that keeps, loses or rasterises the lines that fell inside it and moves as one piece, so its hatching stays whole. What is behind the world is clipped to the gaps, a little inside them, so the colour pen never touches the black.

name: Gear 3D
subtitle: Gears on ripples, rays and ribbons.
tags: perspective rays ripple stream truchet floor gears
description: Solid gears rise out of fields of rays, ripples and ribbons. Camera angle and floor spacing change the composition.
lesson: Perspective projects the gear geometry onto paper. Hidden lines are removed, and floor spacing is constrained so distant detail can still be plotted.

name: Gear reverb
subtitle: Gear trains and offset rings.
tags: echo rings meshing gears field
description: A meshing gear train surrounded by rings of echoes. Explore the space where mechanical geometry becomes a contour field.
lesson: Offset rings radiate from the gear train. Ring spacing, camera angle and the outline of the field change the balance between machinery and landscape.
